lines.text: Today your web page wakes up. You will write JavaScript so buttons react when you click them.
HTML builds the page and CSS styles it.
JavaScript makes it react, like changing words when you click a button.
Every game and app on the web uses it.
JavaScript goes inside a script tag, usually at the very bottom of the page.
The browser builds the page first, then runs the script.
In the Web Lab, the live preview runs your script, so you can click your buttons right away.
Give an element an id, like id equals score.
In JavaScript, document dot getElementById finds that element.
Then you can change its words with textContent, or its colour with style.
The addEventListener command tells a button to listen for a click.
Inside it, you write what should happen each time it is clicked.
That code runs again every single time you click.
A variable is a named box that stores a value, like let score equals zero.
Score equals score plus one adds one to it.
Show the new score on the page and you have a counter.
The script finds the paragraph by its id and stores it in msg.
Then textContent replaces the words, so the page shows a new message.
addEventListener tells the button to wait for a click.
The code inside the curly brackets runs only when the click happens.
The variable called clicks starts at zero before anyone clicks.
Every click adds one, and textContent shows the new number on the page.
JavaScript can change CSS too, using style.
In JavaScript, background color is written as one word with a capital C.
The live preview runs your JavaScript, so you can click your buttons straight away.
If nothing happens, compare each id carefully and make sure every quote mark has a partner.
When it works, press Check to see which goals you have reached.
The id in the script says scor, but the paragraph’s id is score.
JavaScript cannot find it, so check that ids match exactly.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
